overview.body:
**Stribog** ​(*stribog*) ‌— Winds, ‌Storms ​· ​Father ​of ​winds — ​belongs ‌to ​the ​Slavic tradition, ‌where ​it ‌is ​catalogued under ‌the ​domain ​"Winds, ​Storms". ​The name ​means ‌"Father ​of ‌winds".

**Stribog** ​is ‌winds, ​storms. ‌The ​name means ‌"Father ​of ​winds" ‌and belongs ‌to ‌the ​slavic ​tradition.

PuniCodex ‌restores ​the ​name ‌as ​**Stribog** and ​serves ‌its ​temple ‌at [its ​temple](https://punicodex.com/stribog/). ​The ​restoration ​needs ‌no distinctive ‌letters ​or ‌diacritics ​its ASCII ​form ‌would ‌lose, ‌which places ‌the ​name ‌in ​Tier ​2. The ​plain ‌ASCII ​form ​*stribog* survives ​as ‌a ​modern ​convenience ​imposed by ‌the ​early ‌domain-name ​system; the ‌restoration, ​not ‌the ‌fallback, is ​the ​form ​the ​project ‌defends as ‌philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
No ​indigenous written ‌attestation ‌survives for ​this ​name; **Stribog** ​is ​a scholarly ​transliteration ‌of the ​reconstructed ​spoken form. ‌Etymologically ​the name ‌means ​"Father of ‌winds".

​The ASCII ​form ​*stribog* survives ​only ​because the ‌early domain-name ​system ‌could not ​carry ‌diacritics; it ​is ‌a technological ​compromise, ‌not an ​ancient ​spelling. The ‌Unicode ‌restoration **Stribog** ‌recovers ​the full ​diacritic ‌detail of ​the ​scholarly transliteration ‌directly ​in the ​address ‌bar. The ​restoration ‌needs no ​distinctive ​letters or ​diacritics ​its ASCII ‌form ‌would lose, ​which ‌places the ​name ​in Tier ‌2.

‌The letter-by-letter ‌transformation ‌runs:

- ​**s** ‌→ **S** ​— ​Same, capitalized
​- ‌**t** → ​**t** — ​Same
​- **r** ‌→ ​**r** — ​Same
​- **i** ‌→ ​**i** — ‌Same
​- **b** ‌→ ​**b** — ‌Same
‌- **o** ​→ ​**o** — ​Same
​- **g** ‌→ ‌**g** — ​Same

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/stribog/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**stribog** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Stribog.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"stribog" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Stribog".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"stribog" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Stribog" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Stribog was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Stribog ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Stribog ‌place ​winds, storms ​at ​the ​center of ​a ‌living mythological ​world.

​### ‌Origins (Myth)

​Stribog ‌appears ​in slavic ‌tradition ​as winds, ​storms. ​The ​name's meaning, ​"Father ‌of ​winds", shapes ‌the ​narratives told ‌about ​this ‌figure.

### ​Worship ‌and ​Memory (Cult)

​Devotees ‌and later ‌tradition-keepers ‌preserved ​Stribog in ​ritual, ‌text, ​and iconography, ​ensuring ‌the name ​survived ​into ‌the modern ​scholarly ‌record.

​The myths ​of ​Stribog survive ​in ‌fragments, ‌summaries, and ​later ‌retellings. ​Each version ​reflects ‌the interests ‌of ‌its ‌tellers — ​poets, ‌priests, ​philosophers, and ​scholars. ​The PuniCodex ‌entry ​does ​not privilege ​a ‌single ​version; it ​gathers ​the attestations ‌so ​that ‌readers can ​compare ‌them. ​The restoration ‌Stribog ‌gives the ​figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Stribog ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Slavic ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Stribog, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​winds ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Stribog is ‌to ​hold ​the ​idea ​of winds, ​Storms ‌in ​the ​mind ‌and to ​ask ‌what ​of ‌it endures. ​The ​name ​means ​"Father ​of winds" ‌— ​and ‌a ​name that ‌carries ​its ‌meaning ​so ‌openly invites ​meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere ‌recollection. The ​tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name as ​winds, ‌Storms ​· ​Father ‌of winds.

​Sit ‌with ​the ​restored ​form — ​Stribog ‌— ‌and ​the diacritics ‌themselves ​become ​the ‌practice: ‌each mark ‌is ‌a ​small ‌act ​of attention, ​a ​refusal ‌to ​let the ​plain ​ASCII ‌form ​*stribog* ​stand in ​for ‌the ​whole. ‌What the ​tradition ‌preserved ​in ‌this ‌name, the ​restoration ​asks ​the ​reader ‌to preserve ‌in ​turn.
